summary.en: Rebel forces and government troops continue to clash near the Uganda border, killing one and wounding three, while similar fighting in Greater Tonj sees UNMISS patrols protecting civilians. Communal violence has forced 15,000 civilians to flee Gbudwe and 27,000 displaced in Upper Nile as rival groups battle in Lakes state, prompting the detention of 16 community leaders and the launch of peace talks in Tonj East. IGAD is probing the Bentiu attacks, and a drone strike on a market in the disputed Abyei region killed 73 people, according to Addis Standard. The UCDP recorded 2 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Rebelstyrker og regjeringsstyrker fortsetter å kjempe nær grensen mot Uganda, og har drept én og såret tre, mens lignende kamper i Greater Tonj ser UNMISS-patruljer beskytte sivile. Kommunal vold har tvunget 15 000 sivile til å flykte fra Gbudwe og 27 000 til å bli fordrevet i Upper Nile ettersom rivaliserende grupper kjemper i Lakes-staten, noe som har ført til at 16 lokalsamfunnsledere blir arrestert og at fredssamtaler settes i gang i Tonj East. IGAD etterforsker Bentiu-angrepene, og et droneangrep på et marked i den omstridte Abyei-regionen drepte 73 personer, ifølge Addis Standard. UCDP registrerte 2 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
